subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219's bounded longer isolated cron setup watchdog as the canonical fix for this pre-runner timeout class?
rationale: Current source and field evidence support the 60s ceiling as the central failure, but extending setup time changes cron capacity and operator-failure behavior, which is a maintainer policy tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge the open PR after maintainer acceptance that isolated runner setup may occupy a cron slot for longer, capped by the proposed policy.

options.title: Require operator configurability
options.body: Ask for a config-backed watchdog if maintainers want deployments to choose the setup window instead of changing the default policy alone.

options.title: Keep 60s and split backend fixes
options.body: Reject the generic setup-window change and route each provider or harness stall to backend-specific fixes, leaving this issue open until that direction is explicit.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge the open PR after maintainer acceptance that isolated runner setup may occupy a cron slot for longer, capped by the proposed policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history establishing the cron watchdog owner boundary and is the best available routing candidate among the related-code owners for the policy tradeoff.
